name: Tennessee

tn_hope_gpa.label: Tennessee HOPE GPA
tn_hope_gpa.description: Tennessee HOPE GPA: the final overall GPA on a 4.0 scale. Tennessee uses the school's weighted GPA; this estimate is unweighted, so it may be a little low.

programs.name: Tennessee HOPE Scholarship
programs.summary: Lottery scholarship for a 21 ACT (1060 SAT) or a 3.0 GPA: either one is enough. Pays at Tennessee public and eligible private colleges.

also: Tennessee resident for one year before enrolling

award.summary: $2,250 a semester ($4,500 a year) as a freshman and sophomore and $2,850 a semester ($5,700 a year) as a junior and senior at four-year colleges; $1,600 a semester at two-year colleges.

programs.name: General Assembly Merit Scholarship (HOPE supplement)
programs.summary: Adds to HOPE for a 3.75 GPA and a 29 ACT (1330 SAT).

award.summary: An extra $500 a semester ($1,000 a year) on top of HOPE.

programs.name: Aspire Award (HOPE supplement)
programs.summary: Adds to HOPE for students who earn HOPE and whose family income (AGI) is $36,000 or less.

also: Family adjusted gross income of $36,000 or less (from the FAFSA)

award.summary: An extra $750 a semester ($1,500 a year) at four-year colleges; $250 a semester at two-year colleges.

programs.name: Tennessee Promise
programs.summary: Free tuition and fees at Tennessee community colleges and TCATs (colleges of applied technology) after other grants, with a mentor. Apply in the fall of senior year.

award.summary: Tuition and mandatory fees left after Pell, HOPE and state grants, for up to five semesters.

programs.name: Tennessee Student Assistance Award (TSAA)
programs.summary: Need-based grant from the FAFSA. Money runs out each year, so file as early as possible.

award.summary: About $1,000 a semester at public colleges and up to $2,000 a semester at private colleges (draft).

programs.name: Wilder-Naifeh Technical Skills Grant
programs.summary: Grant for students at Tennessee Colleges of Applied Technology (TCATs). No GPA or income requirement.

aid_steps.title: Tennessee Promise application (free community college)
aid_steps.summary: Tennessee Promise has its own short application in the fall of senior year. Apply even if a four-year college is the plan: it keeps a free option open.
how: Apply on the Tennessee Promise site by November 1 of senior year.
File the FAFSA and go to the required meeting with your Promise partner.
Do the community service hours Tennessee Promise asks for before each term.

aid_steps.title: Make sure HOPE shows on your aid offer
aid_steps.summary: Once the FAFSA is on file, the Tennessee college adds HOPE (and any supplement) to the aid offer.
how: Look for Tennessee HOPE on the chosen Tennessee college's aid offer. If it's missing, ask the financial aid office.
HOPE is kept with a 2.75 college GPA at 24 and 48 hours and a 3.0 at 72 and 96 hours (or a 2.75 overall with a 3.0 that semester).

counselor_notes: Tennessee HOPE needs a 21 ACT (1060 SAT) or a 3.0 GPA, not both. Supplements: General Assembly Merit Scholarship (3.75 GPA and 29 ACT, +$1,000 a year) and Aspire (family AGI $36,000 or less, +$1,500). HOPE only pays at Tennessee colleges; file the FAFSA by September 1 for fall.

Tennessee Promise gives free tuition at community colleges and TCATs: apply by November 1 of senior year, file the FAFSA, attend a meeting and do community service. The Dual Enrollment Grant pays for college classes in high school. College for TN (collegefortn.org) is the state planning site.
